sentences.text: Cerasinops hodgskissi is the sole species within the extinct genus Cerasinops, representing a small ceratopsian dinosaur.

The holotype specimen suggests a total length of 2.5 meters and a mass of 175 kilograms, though other estimates place the length at 1.70 meters and height at 0.90 meters with a weight between 13 and 18 kilograms.
This animal featured a wide, thick skull equipped with a parrot-like beak that ended in a strong rim.
The holotype specimen MOR 300 preserves about 80 percent of the skull and skeleton, including most limbs but excluding the hands and tail.
It possessed an extra tooth at the front of the jaw and utilized a unique chewing method compared to other ceratopsians.
Fossils were discovered by Jack Horner in 1983 within the Two Medicine Formation in Montana.
Brenda Chinnery and Jack Horner named the species in 2007, and the specific name hodgskissi honors Wilson Hodgskiss, the landowner where the specimen was found.
Scientists debate whether Cerasinops is a basal ceratopsian or a sister taxon to the family Leptoceratopsidae.
Regardless of the debate, the genus is classified within the family Leptoceratopsidae.
All known specimens come from the lower Two Medicine Formation, dated between 77 and 80.2 million years ago.
The time range for the genus is estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
